title: Approving several pending requests pushes an employee's balance below zero
summary: The balance is only checked when a request is created, and pending requests are not counted. An employee can file several requests that each fit, and a manager can approve all of them, so the employee gets more than 20 days and the balance shows a negative number.
steps: POST /api/requests 2077-05-01..2077-05-15 (15 days) → id B (accepted: pending A not counted)
Log in as ana@acme.example (manager); POST /api/requests/A/approve then /B/approve

expected.text: The second approval is refused because it exceeds the remaining balance (20 − 15 = 5); remaining never goes below 0.

actual: Both approvals return 200; balance for 2077 is {used: 30, remaining: -10}.

how.state: SELECT SUM(days) FROM requests WHERE user_id=3 AND status='approved' AND start_date LIKE '2077%' → 30
how.byDesignCheck: R1 caps entitlement at 20 days per year and R7 forbids requests longer than the remaining balance; R5 defines remaining from approved requests, so the cap must hold at approval time. Not the same cause as AL-2 (day counting) or AL-1 (who may approve): here a real manager approves.

hint: In approveRequest, re-compute balance(db, req.user_id, year) and refuse (400/409) when req.days > remaining.
